results.name: Criss Cross Elbow to Knee
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your hands placed behind your head, elbows pointing out to the sides.
Engage your quadriceps and perform a light jump, crossing your legs in mid-air, and land with your feet crossed and immediately lightly jump back to the starting position.
Lift your right knee towards your left elbow while twisting your torso to bring your left elbow towards your right knee.

Return to the starting position, perform another light jump crossing your legs, and repeat the movement on the opposite side by lifting your left knee towards your right elbow. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your abdominal muscles to twist your torso and lift your knee, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
Perform the movement with control, especially during the jumps and twists, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you twist and lift your knee and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Criss Cross Elbow to Knee is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Criss Cross Jack
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wide apart and your arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder level.
Engage your quadriceps and perform a light jump, crossing your legs in mid-air while simultaneously bringing both arms straight in front of your chest.
Land with your legs crossed and your arms in front of your chest.
Immediately jump again to return to the starting position with your feet wide apart and your arms extended to the sides at shoulder level. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your leg, chest and shoulder muscles to perform the jumps and crosses, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
Perform the movement with control, especially during the jumps, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you cross your legs and arms and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Criss Cross Jack is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Glutes.

results.name: Criss Cross Jump
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wide apart and your arms bent out to the sides at shoulder level and hands facing each other.
Engage your quadriceps and perform a light jump, crossing your legs in mid-air while simultaneously crossing both arms in front of your chest.
Land with your legs crossed and your arms in front of your chest.

Immediately jump again to return to the starting position with your feet wide apart and your arms bent out to the sides at shoulder level and hands facing each other. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your leg, chest and arm muscles to perform the jumps and crosses, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
Perform the movement with control, especially during the jumps, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
results.description: Criss Cross Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Glutes.

results.name: Decline Shoulder Tap
instructions: Begin by placing your feet on a bench and positioning your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart. Your body should be in a decline position with your feet elevated.
Engage your core and ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lift your right hand off the floor and tap your left shoulder, lightly rotate your hips according to the tap side.
Return your right hand to the floor and repeat the movement with your left hand, tapping your right shoulder. Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
Avoid letting your shoulders sag; keep them stable and aligned with your hands.
Use a stable bench to prevent any movement or slipping during the exercise.
results.description: Decline Shoulder Tap is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

results.name: Diagonal Opens
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at the elbows, elbows facing outwards, and hands close to your chest.
Slide your right hand over your left forearm, both arms in an opposite diagonal direction while keeping the elbows bent.
Return your hands to the starting position and repeat the movement by sliding your left hand over your right forearm, extending in the opposite diagonal direction.
tips: Ensure your movements are smooth and controlled to maintain tension and focus on muscle engagement.
Focus on maintaining a rhythmic breathing pattern, inhaling as you extend and exhaling as you return to the start position.
Maintain a slight tension in your core throughout the exercise to help stabilize your upper body.
results.description: Diagonal Opens is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Arms.

results.name: Diagonal Punch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hands in a guard position near your face.
Rotate your torso to the right, and extend your right arm in a diagonal punch across your body.
Return your right hand to the starting position as you rotate your torso back to center.
Repeat the motion with your left arm, rotating your torso to the left to execute a diagonal punch across your body.
tips: Keep your hands up and elbows slightly bent when not punching to protect your face and maintain balance.
Rotate your hips and shoulders fully with each punch to maximize power and engage your core muscles.
Practice the punches slowly at first to ensure proper technique before increasing speed and power.
Exhale sharply with each punch to increase force and stabilize your core.
results.description: Diagonal Punch is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Arms.

results.name: Double Kettlebell Sled Push
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the sled and grip the sled handles.
Lean into the sled at about 45 degrees with your arms extended.
Drive forward with powerful steps through the balls of your feet.
Keep pushing for the set distance.
tips: Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Drive your knees forward.
results.description: Double Kettlebell Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

results.name: Double Knee Drive
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, both arms bent and raised by your sides.
Lift your right knee towards your chest while rotating your torso to the right, bringing your left elbow to touch your right knee twice.
Lower your right leg back to the starting position and return your torso to face forward.

Repeat the movement on the opposite side by lifting your left knee towards your chest, rotating your torso to the left, and bringing your right elbow to touch your left knee twice. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your upper body upright and avoid leaning too far forward or backward to maintain balance and proper form.
Engage your core muscles to stabilize your body and enhance the rotational movement.
Focus on a steady, rhythmic breathing pattern, exhaling as you bring your knee and elbow together.
results.description: Double Knee Drive is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Obliques.

results.name: Double Punch Front Leg Lift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands in fists near your sides with closed fists.
Simultaneously punch forward with both arms while lifting your right leg slightly bent at the knee to about waist height.
Return your arms and right leg to the starting position.
Immediately repeat the movement, this time lifting your left leg while simultaneously punching forward with both arms. Continue alternating leg lifts with each set of punches.
tips: Ensure your punches are strong and controlled, extending fully without locking your elbows.
Maintain a slight bend in the lifted leg to reduce strain and enhance control during the movement.
Focus on a steady, rhythmic breathing pattern, exhaling as you punch and lift your leg, and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Double Punch Front Leg Lift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Arms.

results.name: Downward Dog Sprint
instructions: Begin with your hands shoulder width apart and your feet hip width apart. Walk your feet backward until your body forms an inverted V shape with your hips lifted toward the ceiling.
Keeping your hands firmly planted, flex one knee lifting your foot off the floor while the opposite leg remains extended.
Return your foot to the starting position, then immediately drive the opposite leg in the same way.
Continue alternating legs in a smooth, controlled sprinting motion while keeping your hips elevated and your upper body stable.
tips: Lift each knee toward your chest without rounding your upper back.
Maintain your hips high throughout the exercise instead of shifting into a plank position.
Engage your core to minimize movement through your torso.
Inhale as you return your foot to the floor and exhale as you drive your knee forward.
results.description: Downward Dog Sprint is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps, Hamstrings.
